ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

As an Indirect Procurement Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the Supply Chain Team in conducting market analysis and identifying actionable solutions to optimize costs while maintaining service quality.

- As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally

- Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges

- Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates

- Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events

Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results.

- GPA of 3.0 or above.

- 3+ months of corporate function experience within the areas of supply chain.

- GPA of 3.5 or above.

- 6+ months of corporate function experience within the areas of supply chain.

- Data analytics experience

- Experience with data analysis tools (PowerBI)

- Experience with ERP systems (Infor LN)

- Experience with Python

- Six Sigma experience

- Advance proficiency with Excel

- Supply chain purchasing and procurement experience

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

- Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027

- Pay Range CA: $25.00 USD Hourly

- You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs

$25—$25 USD

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. About Us

Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.

About the Role

The Company

Tracing our roots to 1928, Wellington Management Company, LLP (WMC) is one of the world’s largest independent investment management firms. With over $1 trillion in assets under management, we serve as a trusted adviser to institutional clients and mutual fund sponsors in over 60 countries. Our innovative investment solutions are built on the strength of proprietary, independent research and span nearly all segments of the global capital markets, including equity, fixed income, multi-asset, and alternative strategies. As a private partnership whose sole business is investment management, our long-term views and interests are aligned with those of our clients. We are committed to attracting a talented and diverse workforce, and to fostering an open, collaborative culture of inclusivity because we believe multiple perspectives lead to more informed investment and business decisions. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we welcome people with diverse life experiences, fresh ideas, and specialized subject-matter expertise.

The Position

The People Analytics team at Wellington is seeking a data analytics professional who is motivated by delivering data-driven insights that enable leaders to proactively plan their talent needs; evaluate and strengthen organizational effectiveness; identify past and future trends leveraging predictive analytics; and make informed talent decisions that drive business outcomes. The co-op for this team will bring technical expertise to the team to help build analytical models with practical, valuable applications in areas such as strategic workforce planning, attracting and retaining talent, employee engagement, high-potential talent identification & development, and employee development. This could include AI-driven analytical solutions, consolidating and streamlining dashboards to simplify user experience, improving our data quality and architecture, and building visualization tools to support scalable and automated analytics. This is a hands‑on opportunity for a curious, data‑driven problem‑solver to apply analytical skills in a real‑world HR environment while collaborating closely with partners across Talent, HR, and broader business teams.

As a data-driven organization, this role is critical to advancing our analytical maturity by fully utilizing our HR data lake to predict future trends, identify leading indicators, define data limits, and evaluate program success. We have an exciting roadmap ahead!

Responsibilities

The co-op will have day-to-day responsibility of supporting our People Analytics function with delivering high-quality and reliable monthly and quarterly analytical support, maintaining critical dashboards, and supporting client and ad hoc reporting requests. Additionally, the role will have a few key projects across all areas of human resources to help advance and scale our reporting capabilities. A sample of your responsibilities might include:

- Use your technical expertise in data science to lead the prediction and forecasting workstream and build capabilities within HR and cross-functionally using HR data

- Proposing, testing and validating AI-driven analytical models and technology capabilities to redesign the way we work to be more efficient and effective

- Proactively identify research opportunities by mining data to generate practical talent insights for the business

- Decommissioning and consolidating reporting dashboards from Tableau to PowerBI data visualization

- Perform deep-dive analysis and research to recommend best in class people analytics to drive business success, deliver insights on root causes, drive data consistency, and make recommendations for continuous improvement

- Support operational efficiency by helping to streamline workflows to optimize business processes and implement technology-enabled innovation

Qualifications

- Major in Data Science, Business Analytics, Finance, Economics or related field preferred

- Passionate about HR systems and using data to drive business impact

- Minimum 3.0 GPA

- Value precision, strong attention to detail, and highly organized

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences

- Demonstrated knowledge and/or experience with data visualization, analysis, and programming tools, including Power BI, Tableau, SQL, and Python

- Familiarity with data infrastructure concepts such as automation, APIs, data modeling, and data management, with a willingness to learn and apply these tools to support team goals

- Enterprising, forward-looking, entrepreneurial self-starter attitude

- Proven ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, change-driven environment

- A positive and proactive work ethic, ability to roll up sleeves and get things done

- Inquisitive problem solver with strong project-management skills and ability to meet and prioritize deadlines

- Fit with the firm’s cultural tenets of inclusivity, collaboration, accountability, and collegiality

Please note: This co-op position entails cross-training to ensure optimal performance across functions. The anticipated start date for accepted candidates is December 2026/January 2027.

Only Northeastern University students are eligible for this program.

ABOUT EXODUSPOINT

ExodusPoint Capital, founded in 2017 by Michael Gelband, began managing investor capital in 2018. The firm employs a global multi-strategy investment approach, seeking to deliver compelling asymmetric returns by combining complementary liquid strategies managed by experienced investment professionals within a robust risk framework. ExodusPoint brings together an accomplished team with hands-on experience running multi-manager businesses to create an institutional investment management firm.

The Role

ExodusPoint is looking for a Quantitative Intern to join a Corporate Credit investment team in Philadelphia.

You will work directly with the team’s traders, helping build the analytics and tools they use to monitor markets, identify opportunities and manage risk.

The team trades investment-grade Corporate Credit across new issues and secondary markets. The role will be particularly focused on the quantitative side of the investment process – working with market and trading data, developing analytics, automating existing processes and finding better ways to present information to the desk.

We don’t require previous Credit or finance experience. We are looking for someone who is highly analytical, comfortable coding and interested in applying those skills to a live trading environment.

What You’ll Do

- Build dashboards and analytics for the trading team.

- Analyse market, pricing and trading data.

- Develop tools to identify relative-value opportunities and market dislocations.

- Help improve intraday P&L, position and risk analytics.

- Analyse liquidity and dealer activity across Corporate Credit markets.

- Automate existing data and analytical processes.

- Build and improve data pipelines used by the desk.

- Backtest quantitative ideas and help assess whether they are useful in practice.

- Work directly with traders to understand problems and build practical solutions.

- Use tools such as Claude Code and Codex to improve the speed and efficiency of development.

The work will be driven by problems the team is dealing with day-to-day. We want someone who is comfortable taking an idea or loosely defined problem and figuring out how to solve it.

What We’re Looking For

- Currently studying, or recently completed, a degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Engineering, Data Science or another quantitative field.

- Strong coding skills, particularly Python.

- Experience working with data and quantitative analysis.

- A good understanding of statistics and probability.

- Comfortable using modern coding and AI development tools.

- Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

- Curious, self-motivated and comfortable working independently.

- An interest in markets and trading.

A combination of Computer Science and Mathematics / Statistics would be particularly relevant, although we are open to candidates from a range of quantitative backgrounds.

Graduate-level study is helpful but not required.,You do not need to have worked in Credit or financial markets before.

We care more about whether you can code, work with data and think through quantitative problems. Previous experience or coursework in markets, quantitative finance, machine learning or trading is useful, but not essential.

The Team

You will sit directly with the investment team in Philadelphia and see how the tools you build are used in the trading process.

This is intended to be an in-person, full-time internship lasting approximately 3–4 months. Candidates do not need to currently live or study in Philadelphia, but should be able to work from the Philadelphia office during the internship.

There may be scope for a longer-term opportunity depending on performance and the needs of the team.

Learn more at appliedintuition.com/research.

Supported by industry-leading tools and infra, researchers can access millions of miles of data from large fleets, and deploy methods they develop into various autonomous and robotic systems including self-driving cars/trucks, autonomous mining/construction machines, humanoid robots and dexterous hands. In addition to your research contributions, you will contribute to and learn from best practices in the autonomy and robotics industries within our fast-paced and customer-focused culture. Improvements deployed to our system immediately help our customers with their programs and deliver value to our business.

At Applied Intuition, you will:

- Conduct research on reinforcement learning (RL) related topics including large-scale self-play RL, VLA post-training, large-scale closed-loop RL based on neural simulation with applications to autonomous driving

- Diving into fundamental topics on RL with broader applications and potential imitative behavior learning incorporation, and relevant topics such as reward learning

- Work closely with the Research Scientists and Engineers on high quality research publications for submission to top-tier conferences

We’re looking for someone who has:

- Strong research background and skills on relevant topics, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively on projects

- Current PhD (or MSc) studies in machine learning, computer vision and graphics, robotics

- 1+ year of research experience in autonomy, self-driving, or related field

- Passion for next-generation, scalable autonomy and robotics

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
